tasks.task: Build one game mechanic in Unity

items.when: When the studio has an idea but no written spec for the mechanic or its tuning numbers
When a new mechanic, or one that feels wrong, must go from brief to a merged change
When you write movement, pick-ups, menus or rules from a feel brief, parts list first
When the mechanic must fit a project where designers edit data and systems stay separate
Before coding, to list the cases the mechanic must pass, smallest first
When the mechanic keeps growing, to cut scope and follow what the code really does

tasks.task: Tune how a mechanic feels

items.when: When the client says snappy, floaty or heavy, or names a game, and you need starting numbers
When the feel must serve the game's design pillars and nobody has written them
When the numbers are set, to plan one morning of people playing and what to watch

tasks.task: Fix a physics, input or timing bug

items.when: When a tester sends rough notes and a screenshot and you need a clean issue
When you have the bug and the code near it and need suspects ranked with a check each
When you must reproduce at set frame rates, name the kind of bug and fix it
When the report is vague and needs a repeatable case and a record of what is verified
When the fix needs the cause proven, a test and a pull request
When earlier fixes did not hold and the cause must be proven before code changes

tasks.task: Split a messy script into clear parts

items.when: When the script has no tests and needs a safety net before it is split
When one script does input, movement, health, UI and sound and must become small parts
When game rules hide in scene code and should become plain functions you can test
When the split needs named, small moves that keep behaviour the same
When an AI wrote the script fast, to find the few risks that will hurt later

tasks.task: Write edit mode and play mode tests for game rules

items.when: Before writing tests, to list the odd cases for damage, scoring, cooldowns or inventory
When you want Unity tests for the game's rules and one key behaviour
When the suite is red and you want capped rounds of fixes until green or stopped
When nothing is testable yet, to list the cases and take one small step at a time

tasks.task: Build a save system that survives updates

items.when: When saves need a version number, safe writes and upgrades from every old version
Before changing the save format, to see whose saves break and a safer way to ship it
When the design is drafted, to list how a save could be lost or corrupted
When the plan assumes the game never quits mid-save, to design for when it does

tasks.task: Plan a move to a newer Unity version

items.when: When a project is on an older Unity version and needs a safe, ordered plan
When one package or plugin is the risky part and needs stages with a test each
When the upgraded build is about to ship and needs checks and a way back

tasks.task: Get a game ready to release on Steam

items.when: When a small studio needs a dated timeline counted back from launch day
When it is a first Steam launch or an update big enough for a public beta
When the beta needs who to invite, what to ask and a clear rule for when it ends
When the date is fixed and the feature list is too long to finish
Before each build goes out, for a go or no-go, a version and a changelog
On release day, for checks, a rollback and how to know it worked

tasks.task: Check paid items, odds screens and the age rating

items.when: Before a release that sells anything in the game, most of all random items
When the shop and currencies were never planned and prices need a fair basis
When the game needs a draft privacy notice or terms to send to a lawyer

tasks.task: Build menus, settings and the first-run tutorial

items.when: When new players get lost in the first minutes and need a short guided start
When you write the menu, pause and settings screens and the code behind them
When button labels, prompts and error lines need to be short and clear
When the menus are drafted, to score them and list each usability break

tasks.task: Turn a game idea into a design plan and first prototype

items.when: When an idea needs pillars, a gameplay loop and mechanic specs on paper
When one thing must be tested with three to five features and a short schedule
When several ideas compete and a five-day sketch, build and test would pick one
When the plan is bigger than the team, to keep the core and park the rest

tasks.task: Balance the economy and progression

items.when: When each currency needs its sources and sinks and a balance check over time
When players do not come back, to score the weak steps in the return loop
When the economy sells items, to check it stays fair and inside store rules

tasks.task: Plan levels, pacing and story beats

items.when: When a level needs a brief with pacing and a check that players can find their way
When the game needs a story plan with the paths players can choose
When dialogue is written, to test each line and fix the worst

tasks.task: Find and fix frame rate and memory problems

items.when: When the game stutters and you need CPU, memory and loading hot spots found
When the bottleneck is known and must be fixed and timed before and after
When art assets and rendering, not code, are the likely cost
When tempted to optimise on a hunch, to measure the real frame first

tasks.task: Plan multiplayer and what syncs between players

items.when: When a Unity game needs a plan for who owns what and what syncs
When the game is in Godot and needs its networking and authority designed
When the game is in Unreal and each piece of state needs an owner

tasks.task: Plan or fix gameplay code in Godot or Unreal

items.when: When the studio works in Godot and needs scenes and scripts planned
When a feature is in Unreal and needs its C++ and Blueprint split planned
When a physics or timing bug is in Godot or Unreal and the same method applies

tasks.task: Write a shader or visual effect

items.when: When a Unity effect needs a shader design with render and speed checks
When the effect is hand-written shader code for the web or a custom engine
When the effect is for Godot
When the effect works but its cost on weaker machines must be checked

tasks.task: Plan the sound system and draft sounds and music

items.when: When the game needs a named list of sound events and rules for music that adapts
When a jump, hit or button needs a short placeholder sound of a set length
When a level needs a draft music clip from a description or a melody
When the studio wants to hear a few music directions before hiring a composer

tasks.task: Make placeholder art and sprites

items.when: When the game needs a few art directions to compare before an artist is hired
When a sprite needs variants or a transparent cut-out
When assets must meet size, format and import rules before they go in the project

tasks.task: Run a playtest and sort the feedback

items.when: Before testers arrive, to find blockers and word the tasks neutrally
When a one-morning test with a script and a fix list is enough
When a fuller test needs task scripts, moderator notes and a findings summary
When feedback from testers, forums and reviews needs ranking into what players need
When poor reviews pile up after launch and you must pick what to fix first

tasks.task: Build an editor tool or automate game builds

items.when: When a repeated editor chore should become an asset checker, drawer or import rule
When builds are made by hand and should run from a pipeline with tests first

tasks.task: Write patch notes players can read

items.when: When you have the commits and need them sorted into tidy notes
When players and the team each need the same update told their own way
Before posting, to catch any line that claims a fix the build does not have

tasks.task: Plan price, community and launch outreach

items.when: When the studio must set a launch price from costs, similar games and value
When the game needs a Discord or forum with channels, onboarding and events
When streamers and video makers should be found, briefed and tracked
When launch news needs a media list, pitch emails and a press kit outline

tasks.task: Prepare game text for other languages

items.when: When text is hardcoded and needs moving to locale files with a plan
When strings are translated, to check meaning and that longer words still fit

always.when: At the end of any coding job, to write what changed, why and the proof that it works

helpers.when: When the game ships on iOS or Android and needs store builds, labels and review
When a release needs a full test pass across machines, saves and settings
When the store page needs capsule art, a logo or screenshots laid out
When the launch needs a trailer cut from gameplay footage
When players need daily replies, moderation and updates, not only a plan
When the game needs accounts, leaderboards or a server behind it

gaps: No library item writes Unity C# for a mechanic, a menu or a save system; only the kit does, and library game items are planning agents
No library item reads Unity Profiler output or finds garbage collection spikes, draw call and batching costs
No library item covers Steam release steps: store page, build review, Coming Soon timing, depots and branches
No library item checks loot box odds disclosure, purchase flows or age rating answers by country
No library item offers two or three game feel directions with numbers to compare side by side
No library item writes Unity Test Framework tests or sets up a headless Unity test run in CI
No library item plans a Unity version upgrade or a render pipeline move
No library item covers controller support, key rebinding or accessibility options in games
No library item writes Godot or Unreal gameplay code; the items for those engines only plan
No library item checks placeholder art or sound against the game's style, or their licences, before release
No library item writes a Steam store description, capsule art brief or trailer plan for a game
